Author: Dinesh Kumar Singh
Bench: Dinesh Kumar Singh

Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 6970 of 2020

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Sandeep Kumar Shrivastava,Hemlata Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Rajesh Kumar Mishra
Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J.
1.
Heard Sri Sandeep Kumar Shrivastava, learned counsel for the accused-applicant and Sri Sanjay Singh, learned A.G.A.-I for the State and perused the record.

2. The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the accused-applicant seeking anticipatory bail in anticipation of his arrest in Case Crime No. 262 of 2019, under Section 323, 504,
420, 465, 468, 471, 477{A}, 218 I.P.C. Police Station Khurja Nagar, District Bulandshahr.
3. It transpires from record that applicant Vijay Kumar Yardv was working as Branch Manager in Oriental Bank of Commerce Branch Kabadi Bazar Chauraha, Khurja, District Bulandshahar.

Feeling aggrieved by conduct of applicant as Branch Manager informant Rajesh Kumar lodged an FIR dated 6.5.2019 which was registered as Case Crime No. 262 of 2019, under Sections 323, 504, 420, 465,
468, 471, 477 (A) & 218 I.P.C., P.S. Khurja Nagar, District Bulandshahar.

In the aforesaid FIR two persons namely, Vijay Kumar Yadav (applicant herein) and Satpal Mehta were nominated as named Vijay Kumar Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12335108/
1 accused.

entities.text: Vijay Kumar Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The allegations in the FIR is to the effect that applicant illegally withdrew a sum of Rs.18,000/- form current account of informant and further restraining the informant from opening his Bank Account.
4. Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in above mentioned case crime number.

Applicant is a bank employee and was posted as Branch Manager in Oriental Bank of Commerce in Branch Kabadi Bazar Chauraha, Khurja, District Bulandshahar at the relevant time learned counsel for applicant has invited the attention of Court to the letter dated 1.11.2018 issued by applicant to the informant stating therein that his cash credit account has been converted into N.P.A. category on account of outstanding dues.
He has then invited attention of Court to the letter dated 5.11.2018 whereby information was given by applicant to the first informant regarding deduction of Rs.18,000/- from current account.
He further contends that other allegations made in FIR has been made only to give colour to FIR.
There is no truth regarding the same.

It is then submitted that FIR giving rise to this application for anticipatory bail was lodged on 6.5.2019 but in spite of fact that a period of more than one year has rolled by from the date of lodging of FIR no police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. has been submitted till date.

It is further contends that though the investigation has been continuing since 6.5.2019 but police has not collected any such material upto this stage on the basis of which complicity of present applicant can be said to be established in above mentioned case crime number.
He further contends that investigation is still going and applicant is co-operating with the investigation and therefore, no coercive process has been issued against applicant.
As such custodial arrest of applicant is not absolutely necessary for investigating above mentioned case crime number.

It is lastly urged that applicant has no criminal antecedents to his credit yet there is definite apprehension of his arrest by the police He therefore contends that liberty of applicant be protected by extending the benefit of anticipatory bail in his favour.
5.Per contra, learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for informant have vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.
However, he could not dispute the facts as noted above as well as the factual and legal submissions urged by learned counsel for applicant.

6. It is pertinent to note that the accused applicant was granted interim protection by this Court vide order dated 03.11.2020 and he has not misused the liberty granted to him.
7.
Considering the fact that the accused applicant was granted interim protection by this Court vide order dated 03.11.2020, no purpose would be served in taking the accused applicant in custody.
8. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application is allowed.
